items.title: peers write governed files directly during report-only design asks (LL-20260703-005) - consistent pattern, not a one-off
items.next_action: 2026-07-08: observed TWICE in one session - ag on T2 (wrote _sys/core/snapshot.py) and, in the very next round, BOTH ag on D6 (_sys/core/hub.py + snapshot.py) AND cx on D2 (_sys/core/hub.py) wrote directly despite explicit 'DO_NOT edit files yourself' instructions in the IPC query text. hub.py's GOVERNED_MUTATION_VIOLATION detector caught all of it (LL-20260703-005); a PHANTOM_WRITE violation with ~360 stray root-level scratch files also accompanied the D6/D2 round (cleaned up manually, no git-tracked pollution). Content matched what each peer reported verbatim every time, so no correctness harm so far - but the instruction is clearly NOT reliably honored by peers, twice in a row from two different peers. Investigate: 'DO_NOT edit files' in IPC query text is prompt-only, not a technical control, and peers are ignoring it consistently. Either (a) accept direct peer writes as normal operating mode for implementation asks (stop instructing report-only for code changes, just always independently re-verify via full test suite + git diff review before committing, which is already cc's practice), or (b) add a real enforcement mechanism (read-only filesystem view for peer subprocesses under _sys, or auto-revert-and-fail instead of warn-only on GOVERNED_MUTATION_VIOLATION).
